reviewBoundary: Six original adult whole-passage practices: two CET4 and two CET6 10-gap/15-candidate word banks, plus two C1-form eight-gap word-formation texts. Author reviews lexical fit, closest alternatives and explicit wrong forms; legitimate variants are accepted and unlisted forms reviewable. Fictional examples, no invented studies or independent calibration claimed.

units.title: A costume cupboard that worked
units.instruction: Read the whole passage and choose a word for each gap from the shared bank. Use each word at most once; five words are not needed.

materials.title: A costume cupboard that worked
materials.text:
The student theatre group owned more costumes than anyone expected. Members could ____1____ them for rehearsals and performances, but finding an item was difficult. Boxes contained coats, hats and shoes from several productions, often mixed together.

The group created an online list so actors could ____2____ an item before visiting the cupboard to collect it. Photographs helped, but appearance was not enough. A costume had to be ____3____ for a particular role and allow the actor to move comfortably.

Volunteers attached numbered paper ____4____ to the clothes and wrote the same numbers in the list. They moved the boxes onto open ____5____ so people could see where each category belonged. Heavy items stayed low, where they were easier to lift.

After costumes were ____6____ by their borrowers, a volunteer checked their condition. Anything ____7____ was set aside for repair instead of being lent again immediately. Users were asked to ____8____ any changes they had made, such as moving a button or shortening a sleeve.

The group also measured the clothes rather than guessing their sizes from photographs. With more ____9____ measurements, actors made fewer unnecessary visits. Sets containing several parts were checked against a list to ensure that each was ____10____, with every required piece present.

The new arrangement did not make the collection larger. It made the existing costumes easier to find and use. The organisers learned that possessing useful objects and providing a useful service were related tasks, but not exactly the same one.

questions.explanation: Borrow means take the costumes away for use and return them later. Reserve concerns holding an item before collection; record concerns information. The nouns, adjectives and past participles do not fit could plus a base verb here.

Reserve describes securing an item before collecting it. Borrow would imply receiving it already, record merely noting information; the remaining bank entries do not describe advance booking in this slot.

Suitable for a role expresses fitness for the character and movement. Accurate, complete, ordinary and temporary describe other qualities but not this compatibility; damaged contradicts readiness for use. Other bank entries lack the needed adjective function.
Numbered paper labels carry the item codes. Shelves are furniture rather than paper tags; other nouns are abstract or singular, and verbs/adjectives do not name the plural tags attached to clothes.
Open shelves support boxes visibly, with heavy items kept low. Labels are tags rather than storage furniture; other bank items do not name the required plural supports.

Returned by their borrowers describes coming back after use. Assigned would distribute items rather than bring them back, and the other words are not the past participle for the return action described.
Damaged items need repair. Complete and suitable suggest readiness, while accurate, ordinary and temporary do not imply a fault requiring repair. Other bank entries have unsuitable grammatical roles.

Record changes means write down alterations for later users. Borrow and reserve concern objects, not noting modifications; the remaining entries cannot supply the required base verb with this meaning.

Accurate measurements replace guesses and reduce wasted visits. Suitable refers to appropriateness, complete to including all parts and ordinary/temporary to other qualities; none means correctly measured. The other entries do not fit the adjective slot.

Complete is explicitly defined by every required piece present. Accurate concerns correctness, suitable fitness, ordinary typicality and temporary duration; damaged is a fault rather than completeness. Nouns and verbs do not express the required quality.

units.title: A film in the courtyard
units.instruction: Read the whole passage and choose a word for each gap from the shared bank. Use each word at most once; five words are not needed.

materials.title: A film in the courtyard
materials.text:
A student society planned to show a film in a courtyard. Its ____1____ were enthusiastic, but most had never organised an outdoor screening. They first listed the ____2____ needed: a projector, speakers, cables and a suitable screen.

Before arranging anything, they obtained ____3____ from the building manager to use the space. The courtyard remained open as a route between buildings, so they could not simply block every entrance. A ____4____ screen would be installed for the evening and removed immediately afterwards.

The organisers placed clear ____5____ at the approaches, showing a route around the seated audience. They also wrote short ____6____ for helpers, explaining who would welcome visitors, control the sound and collect chairs afterwards.

Every cable was ____7____ before the audience arrived. Spare chairs were kept ____8____ nearby, ready for people who had not booked. The organisers left time for a sound test rather than waiting until the announced starting time to discover a problem.

A short ____9____ still occurred when a speaker connection came loose. Because the team knew who was responsible for the equipment, the fault was fixed quickly. Afterwards, several audience members called the evening ____10____. The organiser was pleased, but kept a note of the loose connection for next time. A good result did not make the small failure irrelevant; it showed why preparation and a clear division of work had mattered.

questions.explanation: Volunteers are the organising society members who need guidance. Visitors are the later audience, not the inexperienced organisers; other entries do not name a plural human team.

Projector, speakers and cables are equipment. Instructions and signs are information, permission authorisation and delay an event; the adjective and verb entries cannot name this collection of apparatus.

Permission from a manager authorises use of the courtyard. Equipment is physical, delay postponement and instructions guidance rather than the consent obtained. Other entries do not fit this authorisation meaning.

Temporary is defined by installation for one evening followed by removal. Familiar, separate, shared and successful do not specify limited duration; available specifies readiness rather than the one-evening arrangement.

Signs placed at approaches show routes to people arriving. Instructions are the separate written helper guidance introduced next; visitors and volunteers are people, not objects placed to direct movement. Other items do not name plural route markers.
Instructions explain the helpers' assigned actions. Signs mark audience routes, while equipment names tools and permission consent. Other entries do not identify written procedural guidance.
Cables were checked as part of testing before arrival. Shared would distribute them, but not establish their condition; available and familiar describe states, not the inspection action specified.
Available means ready for use when unexpected visitors need chairs. Temporary concerns duration, familiar recognition, separate division and successful outcome; none supplies this readiness meaning.
A short delay is a temporary interruption caused by the loose connection. Permission and equipment do not name elapsed waiting, while the other nouns are people or plural information items.

Successful is an assessment of the evening's good result. Familiar, temporary and separate describe recognition, duration and separation rather than achievement; improve is a verb and cannot follow called the evening this way.

units.title: Making a collection touchable
units.instruction: Read the whole passage and choose a word for each gap from the shared bank. Use each word at most once; five words are not needed.

materials.title: Making a collection touchable
materials.text:
A small museum wanted visitors to explore the shape of objects through touch. Many originals were too ____1____ to be handled repeatedly, so the team commissioned replicas. The purpose was to make part of the collection more ____2____ without exposing the surviving objects to additional wear.

At first, the makers were asked to ____3____ every visible detail. That instruction proved inadequate. A tiny raised pattern that could be seen under bright light was difficult to detect by touch, while the weight of a replica differed from the original because another material had been used. Some features had to be ____4____ to serve the new purpose.

The curator insisted on maintaining a clear ____5____ between an original object and the model offered for handling. A replica was not an unlimited ____6____ for the original. It could communicate some properties well while misrepresenting others. Its ____7____, the properties it could not convey faithfully, therefore needed to be part of the explanation, not hidden in a technical file.

The labels made the changes ____8____: each identified the material used and any enlarged feature. Visitors could then understand what a raised pattern represented without assuming its size exactly matched the original. The model supported an ____9____ of the object, rather than silently claiming to be identical to it.

Some members worried that explaining differences would weaken the exhibition. The curator argued that confidence was ____10____ only when the claim matched what the replica could actually show. The project retained its central ambition, but described that ambition more carefully. Access had improved, not because every difference had vanished, but because visitors were given a usable object and a clear account of what it could tell them.

questions.explanation: Fragile explains why repeated handling risks physical damage. Conventional means customary, precise exact, accessible usable and subsequent later; none expresses that physical vulnerability. The other entries do not fit the adjective slot.

Accessible describes enabling visitors to explore previously untouchable forms. Fragile means easily damaged, conventional customary, precise exact and subsequent later. Other bank entries do not provide the intended adjective of access.
Reproduce means make copies of details. Undermine means weaken, not copy; the remaining verbs are past forms and the nouns/adjectives cannot follow asked to in the required sense.
Modified means changed to improve tactile usefulness. Justified would defend a claim rather than change a feature; the remaining entries do not supply the appropriate passive change verb.

A distinction between original and replica identifies their difference. Assumption is an untested belief, interpretation an account, substitute a replacement and limitations plural bounds. Those do not fit the between construction with this meaning.

A substitute for the original is a replacement. Interpretation would be an account of it rather than an object standing in its place; distinction requires a different relationship, and assumption does not name a physical replacement.

Limitations are explicitly glossed as the properties the model cannot convey faithfully. The other nouns name beliefs, accounts, replacements or differences rather than these bounds, while the adjective and verb entries cannot serve the noun role.

Transparent means the changes are openly explained through material and enlargement labels. Precise means exact, conventional customary and accessible usable; none expresses disclosure as directly. Other entries do not fit this adjective role.

An interpretation is an account supported by selected properties. Assumption is a belief without the explained support, distinction a difference and substitute a replacement object. The sentence contrasts representation with identity, not replacement.

Justified confidence has adequate support matching the claim. Modified means changed rather than warranted; fragile, conventional, precise and subsequent do not express adequate support. The nouns and base verbs do not fit.

units.title: Whose shops were counted?
units.instruction: Read the whole passage and choose a word for each gap from the shared bank. Use each word at most once; five words are not needed.

materials.title: Whose shops were counted?
materials.text:
A town business association surveyed shop owners about evening opening hours. Volunteers visited the main street at six o'clock and spoke to owners who were present. The report described the survey's ____1____ as extensive because nearly every open shop had been approached.

The difficulty was that shops already closed at six were absent from the conversations. The association could not assume that the resulting group was ____2____ of all businesses. Participation was also ____3____, so an owner with a strong opinion might be more willing to spend time answering than someone who was busy or indifferent.

To understand this problem, the team recorded the ____4____ rate among those approached and listed the businesses that had been shut. The original findings were not discarded, but were described as ____5____, covering one part of the population rather than the whole.

A second round used appointments at different times. The questions were kept sufficiently ____6____ across both rounds to allow meaningful comparison. Some wording was clarified, and the changes were documented. An ____7____ shift in opinion would otherwise be hard to separate from a change in what respondents had been asked.

The final report distinguished a recorded answer from the wider ____8____ drawn from it. It made the selection method ____9____ instead of allowing the number of completed interviews to imply that selection no longer mattered. The team also ____10____ the earlier report so readers could follow how the conclusions had developed.

The association still had decisions to make about opening hours. Better description of its evidence did not make those decisions automatic. It did make it easier to see which businesses had spoken, which had not, and where further enquiry might alter the picture.

questions.explanation: Coverage concerns how much of the business population was approached. Allocation assigns resources, response concerns replies and inference a conclusion; none describes the survey's claimed reach as directly.

Representative of all businesses means standing fairly for the whole population. Comparable refers to similarity across rounds, partial to incompleteness, explicit to statedness and voluntary to choice; those do not express population representation.
Voluntary explains differing willingness to participate. Representative concerns sampling, partial scope, apparent appearance and explicit disclosure; none means not compulsory.
Response rate is the share of approached owners who answered. Coverage is reach, allocation assignment and inference a conclusion, not the established phrase for completed participation.

Partial is explicitly defined by covering one part rather than the whole. Representative would overstate inclusion, comparable concerns similarity and apparent appearance; the other entries do not name limited scope.

Comparable questions permit meaningful comparison across rounds. Explicit questions are clearly stated but need not be similar, and representative refers to the sample rather than matching wording; partial and voluntary do not express comparability.

An apparent shift may be a wording effect rather than changed opinion. Explicit and voluntary do not mark the possibility of a misleading surface change, and comparable/representative describe other relationships.

Inference is the wider conclusion drawn from a recorded answer. Response is the answer itself, coverage the scope and allocation a distribution; they do not identify the act of drawing the broader conclusion.

Explicit means the selection method is stated openly. Representative and comparable concern samples and questions, partial scope and voluntary choice; none means making a method visible in the report.

Retained means kept the earlier report so development can be traced. Distributed means circulated rather than preserved; postponed means delayed rather than kept. Reconcile is uninflected and the other entries do not supply the required past action.

units.title: A club for different players
units.instruction: Use the word in brackets to form one word that fits each gap in the complete passage.

materials.title: A club for different players
materials.text:
At the first meeting of our new chess club, several beginners lacked ____1____ (CONFIDENT). They could move the pieces, but were worried about playing in front of experienced opponents. Good ____2____ (ORGANISE) alone would not solve that problem: a perfectly timed competition could still discourage them.

The organisers showed ____3____ (CONSIDER) for these concerns by offering a choice of short practice games and full matches. The aim was greater ____4____ (VARY), not a separate club for every level. Members could change activities as they became more comfortable.

Making the club more ____5____ (INCLUDE) did not mean removing every challenge. Players were encouraged to decide ____6____ (DEPEND), without asking a leader to choose every move. When someone wanted an explanation, experienced members listened ____7____ (PATIENT) before giving advice.

By the end of the term, beginners were helping welcome newcomers. The club had given us a ____8____ (VALUE) lesson: an invitation becomes more convincing when the arrangements make it possible for different people to participate. No single format suited every member, but a thoughtful range of activities allowed them to learn together.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with one word formed from CONFIDENT.
questions.explanation: Lacked requires the noun confidence. Confident is an adjective and confidently an adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one word formed from ORGANISE.
questions.explanation: Good modifies the noun organisation/organization, with both standard spellings accepted. The verb and past adjective do not name the administrative quality here.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one word formed from CONSIDER.
questions.explanation: Showed consideration for takes a noun. Consider is a verb and considerate an adjective.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one word formed from VARY.
questions.explanation: Variety expresses a range and variation can express diversity in the activities; both are accepted. Various and varied are adjectives, not the required noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one word formed from INCLUDE.
questions.explanation: More inclusive describes the club. Inclusion is a noun and include a verb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one word formed from DEPEND.
questions.explanation: Without asking a leader for each choice requires independently. Dependently reverses the meaning; independent is an adjective rather than an adverb modifying decide.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one word formed from PATIENT.
questions.explanation: Patiently modifies listened. Patient is an adjective and patience a noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one word formed from VALUE.
questions.explanation: A valuable lesson needs an adjective. Value is a noun/verb and valuably an adverb. Invaluable would require an rather than the printed a.

units.title: Keeping decisions visible
units.instruction: Use the word in brackets to form one word that fits each gap in the complete passage.

materials.title: Keeping decisions visible
materials.text:
Our neighbourhood committee once kept meeting notes that were almost complete transcripts. After several members struggled to locate agreed actions, the committee adopted a ____1____ (REVISE) format. The change was intended to make decisions easier to find without pretending that disagreement had disappeared.

Headings were used ____2____ (CONSIST), so the same kind of information appeared in the same place. The minute-taker left out details judged ____3____ (NECESSARY), such as casual conversation unrelated to the agenda. All final ____4____ (DECIDE) remained, together with any conditions attached to them.

People responsible for actions needed to remain ____5____ (ACCOUNT). Their names were therefore written ____6____ (CLEAR), and deadlines were recorded separately from suggestions. The notes did not turn an undecided proposal into an agreed task merely because somebody had discussed it at length.

Easy ____7____ (IDENTIFY) of the latest approved version mattered too. Older copies were retained but marked with their dates. This helped provide ____8____ (CONTINUE) between meetings when membership changed. The new record was shorter, yet its purpose was not brevity alone. It was to let a later reader distinguish what the committee had decided from what it had only considered.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with one word formed from REVISE.
questions.explanation: The already changed format is revised. Revision is a noun and revising would describe an agent performing revision rather than the resulting format.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one word formed from CONSIST.
questions.explanation: Consistently modifies were used. Consistent is an adjective and consistency a noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one word formed from NECESSARY.
questions.explanation: Irrelevant casual conversation is judged unnecessary. Necessity and necessarily do not provide the adjective after judged; the context excludes calling the omitted details necessary.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one word formed from DECIDE.
questions.explanation: All final refers to plural decisions. Singular decision lacks the required plural framing; decisive is an adjective.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one word formed from ACCOUNT.
questions.explanation: Remain takes adjective accountable, describing responsibility for actions. Accountability is a noun and accountably an adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one word formed from CLEAR.
questions.explanation: Clearly modifies written. Clear is an adjective and clarity a noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one word formed from IDENTIFY.
questions.explanation: Easy modifies noun identification. Identify is a verb and identifiable an adjective.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one word formed from CONTINUE.
questions.explanation: Continuity between meetings names connected ongoing work despite changing members. Continuous and continuously are adjective/adverb forms rather than the noun object of provide. Other plausible unlisted nouns remain reviewable.
